category_title: Low-achieving students who are ignored or disengage during group activities
minimal_context: The student is working in a mixed-ability group on a multiple-choice test to ensure all members understand the lessons.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please work with your group on this multiple-choice test. The goal is to make sure that every member understood the lessons.

STUDENT: The better students went faster and they did not always clearly explain information to me.

TUTOR: Have you tried asking them for additional explanations?

STUDENT: I won't risk asking for additional explanations. I feel uncomfortable when I express my ideas because they just 'jumped into my mouth' when I get stuck.

TUTOR: You should still try to contribute to the group's answers.

STUDENT: Why do they always have to recheck my work? I feel devalued when other members revise what I’ve done. The group decisions are mostly made by only one or two members, so I'm put into a jobless situation where I have nothing to do but listen passively or fall to sleep.

options.A: Walk around the room and stand directly behind the student during the group activity.
options.B: Divide the group tasks, then assign different tasks to suitable members during the activity.
options.C: Ignore the student during the group activity, where it is safe to do so.
options.D: Use quiet time, having the student withdraw from the group environment for a time-limited period.
